title: De la mano de: gracias a la intervención de alguien o algo

sections.content: De la mano de (literally "by the hand of") means thanks to, through, or with the direct involvement of a particular person, group, or force. It introduces the agent or means behind an event, often one that drove the change decisively. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Fujimori aplicó, de la mano de un severo programa de ajuste conocido popularmente como el "Fujishock", una drástica eliminación de subsidios y control de precios.
items.english: Fujimori implemented, through a severe adjustment program popularly known as the "Fujishock", a drastic elimination of subsidies and price controls.

items.spanish: Fujimori sorprendió de nuevo al país entero al disolver, de la mano del entonces comandante general del Ejército, Nicolás de Bari Hermoza Ríos, el propio Congreso peruano que lo había investido.
items.english: Fujimori surprised the whole country again by dissolving, with the direct involvement of the then Army commander general, Nicolás de Bari Hermoza Ríos, the very Congress that had installed him.

items.spanish: De la mano de un exitoso operativo de inteligencia policial, las autoridades peruanas lograron capturar a Abimael Guzmán.
items.english: Through a successful police intelligence operation, Peruvian authorities managed to capture Abimael Guzmán.

items.spanish: Estos dos episodios consolidaron, de la mano de una economía finalmente estabilizada tras el llamado "Fujishock", una enorme popularidad inicial para Fujimori.
items.english: These two episodes cemented, together with an economy finally stabilized after the so-called "Fujishock", enormous initial popularity for Fujimori.

sections.content: De la mano de always takes de before its noun -- de la mano del (de + el), de la mano de la, de la mano de un/una. It can point to a person ("de la mano de Hermoza Ríos") or a thing ("de la mano de una reforma").
